blocks.content: containerd is the industry-standard container runtime daemon that actually manages image transfer, storage, and container execution, sitting directly beneath dockerd in the stack covered back in the Docker Engine topic.
1. Where It Sits in the Stack
blocks.text: 1. Where It Sits in the Stack

blocks.content: As introduced in the Docker Engine topic, dockerd does not directly create containers itself, it delegates that work to containerd, which in turn delegates the lowest-level execution work to runc, covered in the next topic.

blocks.alt: One layer below dockerd, one layer above runc

blocks.content: containerd owns three core responsibilities: transferring and storing images (the actual pull/push mechanics), executing containers, and supervising them once running, restarting a crashed process's tracking, reporting status, and so on.

blocks.alt: Image handling, execution, and ongoing supervision

blocks.content: This is a genuinely important fact: containerd is not something Docker built for its own private use, it is a separate, CNCF-hosted project that Kubernetes itself can use directly as its container runtime, entirely independent of Docker.

blocks.alt: Used by Docker, and used directly by Kubernetes too

blocks.content: A small companion process, containerd-shim, sits directly between containerd and each running container, its job is specifically to keep that container running even if containerd or dockerd itself gets restarted or upgraded, a real operational benefit: upgrading Docker does not have to mean restarting every running container.

blocks.alt: Containers keep running through a daemon restart, because of this

blocks.content: containerd is a graduated project under the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (the same governance tier as Kubernetes itself), reflecting its status as stable, widely adopted, foundational infrastructure, not an experimental or Docker-proprietary component.

blocks.alt: A CNCF graduated project, the same tier as Kubernetes

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: containerd sits between dockerd and runc, handling image transfer/storage, execution, and ongoing supervision of containers.
It is a separate, CNCF-graduated project used directly by Kubernetes too, not a Docker-specific internal component.
